message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory protections and responsibilities under the Texas Property Code and related laws. Below is an overview of key rights you typically enjoy as a renter: | Category | Typical Rights (and some responsibilities) | |----------|-------------------------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit and two months’ rent for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep premises safe, sanitary, and structurally sound.
• Must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, and other essential services. | | **Repair & Maintenance** | • If landlord fails to repair, you may withhold rent (in certain circumstances) or pay yourself and deduct from rent.
• You must give reasonable notice before withholding or paying. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot disturb your peaceful use of the property without cause. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑payment of rent: 3‑day written notice.
• For lease termination: 30‑day notice if you’re staying longer than 1 year; 60‑day if less. | | **Eviction Process** | • Must follow court procedures; no “self‑help” evictions allowed. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must give at least 24 hours’ notice before entering, except emergencies. | | **Discrimination** | • Protected against discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, etc. | | **Lease Terms** | • Must be in writing if over 12 months. | | **Rent Control** | • No statewide rent control; local ordinances may apply. | ### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of all communications, receipts, and photos of any damage or maintenance issues. 2. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – Ensure it complies with Texas law; illegal clauses can be voided. 3. **Know When to Seek Legal Help** – If disputes arise, consider contacting a local tenant advocacy group or attorney. If you’d like a sample lease or a more detailed explanation tailored to a particular situation (e.g., furnished vs. unfurnished, short‑term rental), let me know!
